question: Which of the following biodiversity hotspots is NOT present in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wallacea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wallacea is a biodiversity hotspot that includes islands in Indonesia and is not found in India.
 
• The region is named after Alfred Russel Wallace, a British naturalist who independently conceived the theory of evolution through natural selection.
 
• Wallacea is known for its unique flora and fauna, including many endemic species that are not found anywhere else in the world.
 
• This biodiversity hotspot is located between the Asian and Australian continental plates, leading to a mix of species from both regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biodiversity Hotspots**

 
 
• Biodiversity hotspots are regions with a high level of endemic species that are under significant threat from human activities.
 
• There are 36 recognized biodiversity hotspots worldwide, each holding at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics and having lost at least 70% of its original habitat.
 
• These areas are critical for conservation efforts as they contain a large proportion of the world's biodiversity in a relatively small area.
 
 
 
• **Sundaland**
 
 
• Sundaland includes the Malay Peninsula, Borneo, Sumatra, Java, and the surrounding small islands.
 
• It is one of the most biologically diverse regions in the world and is part of the Indo-Malayan realm.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**
 
 
• The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India.
 
• This region is known for its rich biodiversity, including many endemic species of plants and animals.
 
• It is one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Burma**
 
 
• The Indo-Burma region extends across parts of northeastern India, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam.
 
• It is one of the most biologically diverse areas in the world, with a high number of endemic species.
 
• This hotspot faces significant threats from habitat destruction and fragmentation.
